say: Let's find out why the Moon changes shape.

do.text: Why does the Moon have phases?

say: Here is the Sun, far away on the left, lighting everything it shines on.
In the middle is the Earth, where we stand looking up at night.
The Moon goes round the Earth once in about a month.

do.text: One trip round the Earth takes about $29.5$ days

say: The half of the Moon that faces the Sun is ALWAYS lit, wherever it is.

do.text: The Sun always lights HALF of the Moon

say: What changes is how much of that lit half we can see from here.

do.text: We see more or less of the lit half

say: Now let us name the phases, one at a time.
When the Moon is between us and the Sun, we see only its dark side: a new moon.

do.text: New moon: the dark side faces us

say: A week later we see half of the lit side, and two weeks later all of it: a full moon.

do.text: Full moon: the lit side faces us

say: Look back at our first drawing: one trip round the Earth is the whole set of phases.

ask: So when the Moon is between us and the Sun, which half faces us?
